standard.name: complete randomization with a fixed treatment count

assumptions.condition: \(Q(z\mid x)\le\lambda Q(z\mid x')\) for every \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\) and every report \(z\).

novel.justification: The condition models a trial in which an assignment service sends each participant a treatment and the analyst receives only locally privatized reports; client-side telemetry and secret-shared assignment services instantiate this separation.

definitions.name: fixed-channel exact-confidence program
definitions.construction: \(V_m(Q)=\min_{0\le c\le1,\ell}\ell\) subject to \(\sum_hP_{n,m,Q}(h)c_{h,\tau(n)}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sum_{h,t}P_{n,m,Q}(h)c_{h,t}\le\ell\) for every \(n\in\mathcal O_N\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal A_\lambda\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_\lambda=\{a\in\mathbb R_+^{14}:\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq\mathcal X}a_S[1+(\lambda-1)\mathbf 1\{x\in S\}]=1\ \text{for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf G_m(\lambda,\alpha)\)
definitions.construction: Factor \(P_{n,m,Q_a}(h)=\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)a^h\) and minimize \(\ell\) over \(a\in\mathcal A_\lambda\) and \(d\) subject to \(0\le d_{h,t}\le a^h\), \(\sum_h\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)d_{h,\tau(n)}\ge1-\alpha\), and \(\sum_{h,t}\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)d_{h,t}\le\ell\) for every \(n\in\mathcal O_N\).

definitions.name: \(\Gamma_J\)
definitions.construction: Extract a fixed channel-support and confidence-active-set description from \(\mathsf G_m(\lambda,\alpha)\); solve its algebraic stationarity and complementary-slackness equations; then certify every inactive slack and global polynomial residual on \(J\) by facewise identities, Bernstein or Handelman coefficients, or a Fritz John strengthened sum-of-squares certificate.

statements.statement: For every \(N,m,\alpha,\lambda\) and every admissible finite-output \(Q\), symmetrizing the confidence rule reduces schedules to \(\mathcal O_N\) and transcripts to \(H\) with exact law \(P_{n,m,Q}\). Moreover, there exist \(a\in\mathcal A_\lambda\) and an input-independent postprocessing kernel \(K\) such that \(Q=Q_aK\), so \(V_m(Q_a)\le V_m(Q)\). For fixed \(Q\), the fixed-channel exact-confidence program and its finite least-favorable-prior dual have equal attained values.
statements.justification: This theorem turns an infinite-output private confidence-design problem with \(4^N\) schedules into a finite exact decision game without discarding composite schedule nuisance.
statements.gap: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath treat convex column-separable utilities, Rigdon and Hudgens treat exact SATE inference without privacy, and Schafer and Stark fix the experiment; none proves their joint reduction.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite certified optimization layer required by a hidden-assignment A/B-testing protocol to return schedulewise exact SATE confidence sets.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(N,m,\alpha,\lambda\), \(\inf_QV_m(Q)\) equals the attained optimum of \(\mathsf G_m(\lambda,\alpha)\), whose only nonlinear constraints are \(d_{h,t}\le a^h\) of degree \(N\). The graph of \(L^\star_{N,\alpha}(\lambda)\), the gap \(\Delta_{N,\alpha}(\lambda)\), and the set \(\mathcal B_{N,\alpha}\) are semialgebraic; for fixed \(N,\alpha\), \(\mathcal B_{N,\alpha}\) is a relatively closed finite union of intervals and points.
statements.justification: Attainment and semialgebraicity make an exact phase boundary a legitimate finite algebraic target rather than a numerical heuristic.
statements.gap: Generic polynomial optimization yields existence machinery, but the degree-\(N\) lifting and equality-set formulation are specific to the common-channel exact-confidence game.
statements.consumer: The result reduces mechanism selection at algebraic privacy and coverage levels to finite certificate verification and isolates a finite list of possible design-regime changes.

statements.statement: At \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and \(\lambda=1000\), \(129113957/50000000\le L^\star_{4,2/5}(1000)\le64557127/25000000\), every global optimizer uses \(m=2\), and \([999.9,1000.1]\cap\mathcal B_{4,2/5}=\varnothing\). In particular, no balanced randomized response after a nontrivial binary partition is globally optimal throughout that interval. Separately, at \(N=4\), \(m=2\), \(\lambda=3\), and \(\alpha=1/10\), the mapping \(Q\mapsto-V_2(Q)\) is not convex, so the confidence objective is not representable by the convex-utility premise used for the generic extreme-point shortcut.
statements.justification: The certified interval rules out a universal binary-optimality story and places the boundary search on a genuinely nontrivial equality set.
statements.gap: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath and Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa prove binary or partition structure for single-draw divergence objectives, not this fourfold composite-confidence loss.
statements.consumer: A protocol designer at these parameters must retain at least a nonbinary candidate family rather than restricting the acquisition layer to one-bit randomized response.

statements.statement: Fix \(N=4\). On any cell \(J\) on which the channel support, confidence-primal basis, confidence-dual basis, and signs of the dual positive parts are fixed, membership \((\lambda,\alpha)\in\mathcal B_{4,\alpha}\) is equivalent to the existence of a certificate \(\Gamma_J\) that simultaneously verifies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementary slackness, channel stationarity including active privacy faces, and nonnegativity of every residual polynomial over the whole staircase polytope. Every boundary point internal to the projection of \(J\) is a real root of a determinant, inactive-slack, residual-contact, or candidate-value-difference polynomial generated by \(\Gamma_J\).
statements.justification: This is the exact optimality certificate and finite boundary-candidate theorem needed to turn a phase diagram into mathematics.
statements.gap: Mai supplies generic finite-convergence conditions, while the present equivalence must fuse a confidence LP saddle, privacy-face stationarity, and global residual positivity without assuming a rational optimizer.
statements.consumer: It gives an independently checkable certificate format for choosing a private trial design and for auditing the privacy budget at which the optimal channel family changes.

statements.statement: For \(N=4\), determine a nonempty two-dimensional parameter cell \(J\), an explicit optimizing channel family, and an attaining certificate \(\Gamma_J\) for which one algebraically isolated endpoint lies on the boundary of \(\mathcal B_{4,\alpha}\); prove the sign of \(\Delta_{4,\alpha}(\lambda)\) on both adjacent cells and identify which channel support or confidence active set changes at that endpoint.
statements.justification: An actual optimizer-attaining cell and sign-certified endpoint are the nonroutine content that separates a structural design theorem from a high-precision numerical bracket.
statements.gap: No cited work identifies a boundary for a common-channel, exact finite-population causal confidence game; the presolve evidence establishes only exclusion and a narrow value bracket near \(\lambda=1000\).
statements.consumer: The endpoint yields an operational rule for when a one-bit hidden-assignment reporting protocol ceases to be minimax and a richer local report must be deployed.

statements.statement: At \(\lambda=1\), every admissible channel is input-independent and \(L^\star_{N,\alpha}(1)=(2N+1)(1-\alpha)\). If privacy is removed, \(Q\) is the identity channel, and assignment is revealed, the orbit program reduces to exact binary-outcome randomization-test inversion for the finite-population SATE.
statements.justification: The two boundary reductions verify that the proposed game agrees with the uninformative experiment and the classical nonprivate exact-randomization problem.
statements.gap: These reductions are sanity checks rather than novelty claims; their role is to prevent the private game from silently changing the causal target or coverage notion.
statements.consumer: They calibrate software tests at the privacy extremes and connect the private procedure to established exact SATE inversion.

sampling_model.design: Complete randomization draws \(W\) uniformly from assignments with exactly \(m\) treated units; the design variable includes the integer \(m\) and the common local channel \(Q\).
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) labeled units and both binary potential outcomes are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The private input \((W_i,Y_i(W_i))\) belongs to \(\mathcal X\), and the analyst does not separately observe \(W_i\) or \(Y_i(W_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The treatment count obeys \(1\le m<N\); no propensity model is estimated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the full finite schedule orbit \(n\in\mathcal O_N\); inference imposes coverage for every orbit and does not estimate a superpopulation regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A finite family of extremal mechanisms, which we call staircase mechanisms, contains the optimal privatization mechanism.
Using a customized privacy mechanism, we can match the lower bound, giving minimax optimal inference.
Both of the resulting \(1-\alpha\) confidence sets are exact.
Inverting the likelihood ratio test minimizes the probability of including false values in the confidence region.
The same non-asymptotic confidence intervals hold for the sample average treatment effect.
We provide a sequence of values, returned by semidefinite programs, finitely converges to the minimal value.
Every extreme point of the fixed-output joint range is attained by a sort--partition--randomize mechanism.

tldr: Exact finite-population causal inference under local privacy is formulated as a joint choice of treatment count, common channel, and randomized confidence rule. Schedule permutation and a constructive Blackwell refinement reduce the problem to a fourteen-pattern, degree-\(N\) polynomial game with an inner exact confidence linear program. The four-unit game already has a certified nonbinary regime and a global value bracket. The paper's kernel is an optimizer-attaining algebraic certificate that persists on a nonempty parameter cell and locates an actual endpoint of the region where balanced binary-partition randomized response is globally optimal.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal local-privacy theory optimizes population estimation risk or asymptotic confidence width, exact randomization inference fixes a nonprivate observation experiment, and staircase optimality applies to convex single-draw utilities. Their intersection leaves the exact common-channel SATE confidence game and its design boundaries unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary schedule, complete-randomization orbit structure, and four protected input values make the causal nuisance finite while preserving the nonconvex product-channel difficulty.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a lossless orbit and channel reduction, exact primal--dual confidence inference, an attained polynomial formulation, certified nonbinary evidence, and an algebraic continuation method culminating in one sign-certified balanced-binary phase boundary.

related_work: Ohnishi and Awan (2025) provide the causal-local-privacy motivation and distinguish joint from customized privatization, but their targets are population MSE and plug-in inference. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) provide exact finite-population SATE inversion with binary outcomes when the assignment and observed outcomes are available. Schafer and Stark (2009) provide the least-favorable-prior view of minimax expected-size confidence regions for a fixed experiment. Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016) provide the staircase geometry for convex column-separable privacy utilities; their proof does not cover the optimized common-channel confidence value. Chen, Cormode, Bharadwaj, Romov, and Ozgur (2024) treat privacy mechanism and allocation as an experiment-design problem under distributed privacy, but do not derive exact schedulewise phase boundaries. Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa (2026) identify sort--partition--randomize mechanisms for simple binary testing, while the present nuisance contains many schedule nulls and no common likelihood-ratio ordering. Mai (2023) informs the exact positivity machinery, and Bienstock, Del Pia, and Hildebrand (2023) caution that algebraic rather than rational certificates may be necessary.
technical_internal_limitation: At \((N,\alpha,\lambda)=(4,2/5,1000)\), the independently reproduced unrestricted bounds differ by \(5.94\times10^{-6}\). This certifies the value to positive tolerance and excludes all unbalanced allocations and balanced binary partitions nearby, but it does not identify a globally minimizing channel. The continuation handle must close this mathematical gap rather than report additional decimal precision.
honest_scope: The orbit kernel, fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, fixed-channel primal--dual program, degree-\(N\) attainment, nonconvexity diagnostic, and the displayed four-unit certificates have concrete derivations or exact finite checks that must be rewritten as proofs. The optimizer-attaining cell and actual boundary are open. The project does not claim four-output sufficiency, general-\(N\) balance, practical gains at \(95\%\) coverage, or equivalence to a protocol that reveals assignment. At \(\lambda=1\) the value reduces to \((2N+1)(1-\alpha)\); without privacy and with revealed assignment the setup reduces to classical exact SATE randomization inversion.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 2 and 4 with the polytope proof in Section 7, and Section 6 discussion were read. The proof first bounds the output alphabet for convex utilities and then exposes staircase columns through a finite linear program.
seed_details.kernel: For \(N=4\), derive an optimizer-attaining primal--dual polynomial certificate on a nonempty \((\lambda,\alpha)\)-cell and use its sign-changing algebraic residual to locate an actual boundary of the balanced-binary equality set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The staircase linear objective in Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath is replaced by the lower envelope of exact confidence linear programs after a common channel is composed four times; the first new step is a simultaneous confidence-dual factorization whose residual is certified on a channel cell.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for exact locally private SATE confidence sets, common-channel polynomial games, and active-set phase-boundary continuation returned causal-LDP estimation, distributed-DP intervals, and generic polynomial optimization, but no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Exact reruns verify a fourteen-pattern reduction, a width \(5.94\times 10^{-6}\) unrestricted bracket at \((N,\alpha,\lambda)=(4,2/5,1000)\), and strict exclusion of all balanced binary partitions on \([999.9,1000.1]\).
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath because staircase utilities reduce to a finite linear program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their reduction requires a convex column-separable utility, whereas the exact confidence value after fourfold channel composition is neither column-separable nor convex; an exact counterexample verifies the failed convexity premise.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Lemma 4 and its private-mean reduction proof, Theorem 6 and its central-limit proof, and Section 7 concluding remarks were read. The paper separates joint and customized privatization but works with population MSE and plug-in intervals.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly when hiding assignment in a common local channel, revealing assignment, and permitting treatment-aware outcome channels have equal minimax exact SATE confidence risk, with a certified positive gap off the equality region.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the private-mean least-favorable subproblem in Ohnishi and Awan by a Blackwell comparison of finite transcript experiments indexed by complete potential-outcome schedules.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing hidden assignment with exact randomization confidence and local privacy found joint privatization estimators and cryptographic trial protocols, but no equality-or-separation theorem for schedulewise exact confidence risk.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The orbit kernel distinguishes schedules with the same SATE, and the operational protocol difference is visible as the analyst sigma-field changes when assignment is hidden.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Blackwell ordering because revealing assignment is always more informative.
seed_details.rebuttal: One dominance direction is immediate, but equality and strictness require a complete characterization of when the extra assignment signal changes this composite-nuisance confidence decision game.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, the pure-privacy staircase theorems and proofs, the approximate-privacy operational argument, and the discussion were read. The paper explicitly notes that its pure-privacy techniques do not transfer to approximate privacy.
seed_details.kernel: For four protected inputs, decide whether \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-local privacy admits a finite universal Blackwell refinement for the exact SATE game, or exhibit a larger-output extreme channel with a strict exact-risk certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The two-level conic layer decomposition of each pure-private column fails when additive \(\delta\)-slack permits input-dependent zeros; the replacement step must classify feasible perturbations of four-row approximate-private channels.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found complete approximate-private extreme-point classifications only for two and three inputs and new star configurations beyond that range, but no four-input causal decision result.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Rawat, Vajha, Kurri, and Sarwate prove the small-input classifications and place four inputs immediately beyond the characterized frontier.
seed_details.red_team: A generic finite-dimensional polytope argument already bounds the required output size.
seed_details.rebuttal: The union over arbitrary output alphabets is not a single fixed polytope, and approximate privacy admits extreme configurations whose output size can exceed the input size.

seed_details.anchor_read: Theorem 2, Theorem 4, their Section 7 proof, and the concluding discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the parameter region in which an optimal exact SATE channel can be chosen with at most four active staircase outputs, and construct a certified region requiring more than four otherwise.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Caratheodory-style output sparsity can no longer be invoked after the confidence rule is optimized, so one must analyze supports of the common-channel polynomial saddle directly.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for output-cardinality bounds under product-channel exact confidence loss found only convex-utility or single-draw divergence results.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Four-ary randomized response is a strong feasible witness, but the verified nonconvexity result removes the standard extreme-point shortcut.
seed_details.red_team: At most four outputs follows from vertices of the four-row staircase normalization polytope.
seed_details.rebuttal: Minimizing the optimized fourfold confidence value over that polytope need not attain a vertex because the negative value is not convex.
seed_details.decision: dropped after ranking because the required-support side has weaker evidence than the boundary seed

seed_details.anchor_read: The randomized-experiment setup, minimax lower bound, estimator theorems, and concluding mechanism-design discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a nondegenerate \((N,\alpha,\lambda)\)-region on which balanced complete randomization minimizes exact private SATE confidence cardinality among all treatment counts.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace population treatment-probability optimization with comparison of finite hypergeometric orbit experiments across integer treatment counts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for optimal allocation under local privacy found asymptotic variance and distributed-privacy budget allocation, not schedulewise exact minimax cardinality.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The exact identity-experiment lower bound excludes \(m=1,3\) for \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and every \(\lambda\ge 1000\).
seed_details.red_team: Balance follows from the reflection \(m\leftrightarrow N-m\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Reflection gives equality only between paired allocations and supplies no monotonicity toward the center.
seed_details.decision: dropped after deepening because the available proof is restricted to one four-unit regime

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, finite-sample mechanism-design discussion in the conclusion, and the frequentist interval construction were read.
seed_details.kernel: Certify a practically conventional coverage cell, including \(1-\alpha=0.95\), on which every binary-partition randomized-response channel is strictly suboptimal for exact SATE confidence cardinality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace plug-in Wald width with an exact schedulewise confidence linear program and a uniform binary-channel dual lower certificate.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for high-coverage exact local-private SATE comparisons found no nonbinary-mechanism theorem.
seed_details.direct_evidence: A strict nonbinary interval is exact-certified at \(1-\alpha=0.6\), but no evidence yet transfers it to \(0.95\).
seed_details.red_team: The existing \(60\%\)-coverage witness should persist by continuity to \(95\%\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuity is local in \(\alpha\) and gives no bridge across a change of \(0.35\), where the confidence active set can change repeatedly.
seed_details.decision: dropped because the evidence is too remote from conventional coverage

seed_details.anchor_read: The high- and low-privacy mechanism theorems, their proofs, and the discussion of correlated data were read.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a large-\(N\) phase limit for the exact-cardinality optimal channel and treatment fraction, with a finite-sample approximation bound to the limiting design game.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The i.i.d. divergence objective must be replaced by a large-deviation or local-asymptotic analysis of hypergeometric schedule orbits under an optimized exact-confidence decision.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing local-private experiment design with finite-population exact-confidence asymptotics found minimax MSE and distributed-DP interval-width results only.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The finite polynomial game exists for every \(N\), but its dimension and certificate cost grow rapidly and no limiting variational form is yet derived.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine asymptotic approximation to the finite game.
seed_details.rebuttal: The adversarial schedule orbit and changing confidence active sets prevent direct reduction to an i.i.d. divergence or a fixed smooth loss.
seed_details.decision: dropped as infeasible for the first specialization

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorem 1 on Bayes--minimax duality, the Monte Carlo convergence theorem and proof, and the final proof discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly when auxiliary randomization strictly reduces minimax expected cardinality relative to deterministic exact SATE confidence sets under a fixed local channel.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace continuous parameter-space test inversion by the finite box of conditional inclusion probabilities and compare it with its integral vertices.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for integrality gaps in exact randomized confidence sets under local privacy found general randomized confidence constructions but no SATE-channel characterization.
seed_details.direct_evidence: At an uninformative channel, randomization attains \((2N+1)(1-\alpha)\), whereas a deterministic exact rule must report the full grid.
seed_details.red_team: The result is a one-line consequence of convexifying deterministic confidence rules.
seed_details.rebuttal: Strictness at the uninformative boundary is immediate, so a publishable characterization would require the full channel-dependent integrality frontier; current evidence does not support that frontier.
seed_details.decision: dropped because the strongest available fact is boundary-trivial

seed_details.anchor_read: The common noninteractive model, Section 6 discussion of interactive extensions, and the Blackwell operational argument for approximate privacy were read.
seed_details.kernel: Determine whether interaction or public assignment-dependent channel selection strictly lowers exact minimax SATE confidence cardinality relative to a common noninteractive channel.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The product of a single common channel must be replaced by a transcript kernel adapted to prior privatized reports, eliminating the finite monomial lifting.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for interactive local-private causal randomization inference found interactive testing separations but no finite-population exact SATE confidence design.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Protocol-information results show interaction can matter in local testing, but no tractable exact reduction is available for this schedule game.
seed_details.red_team: Known interactive local-privacy separations transfer directly.
seed_details.rebuttal: Those separations concern distribution testing or estimation, not schedulewise exact coverage under complete randomization and a causal estimand.
seed_details.decision: dropped as too broad for a first paper

seed:attaining-boundary-certificate: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016) reduce convex column-separable pure-LDP utilities to staircase linear programs and prove binary or randomized-response optimality only in selected privacy regimes.
Schafer and Stark (2009) establish Bayes--minimax duality for expected-size confidence regions and approximate least-favorable mixtures, but do not optimize a data-acquisition channel.
Mai (2023) proves finite convergence of Fritz John strengthened moment--SOS relaxations under finite-critical-value conditions, furnishing a positivity method rather than a causal decision theorem.

Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa (2026) prove sort--partition--randomize optimality for two fixed input distributions and \(f\)-divergences; their conclusion leaves composite and broader objectives open.

The exact target--method search found no paper that couples schedulewise randomization coverage, common four-input local channels, and algebraic continuation of an optimizer-attaining confidence dual.
seed:hidden-assignment-comparison: Ohnishi and Awan (2025) distinguish joint and customized local privatization and derive population minimax MSE and plug-in inference.
Blackwell (1953) supplies the experiment-comparison criterion through stochastic garbling.
Acharya, Canonne, Freitag, and Tyagi (2019) show that protocol information and public randomness alter locally private testing performance.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) provide the revealed-assignment exact randomization endpoint without privacy.
No closer source gives equality and strict-gap regions for hidden-assignment exact SATE confidence risk.
seed:approximate-private-output-frontier: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016) state that their pure-privacy staircase techniques do not extend directly to approximate privacy.
Rawat, Vajha, Kurri, and Sarwate (2026) completely characterize \((0,\delta)\)-local-private extreme points only for two and three inputs and construct new larger-alphabet configurations.
Elangovan and Jog (2024) show qualitatively new \((0,\delta)\)-private extreme geometry and output sizes beyond pure-private analogies.
Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2025) provide fast exact nonprivate SATE inversion, not approximate-private channel geometry.
No source subsumes the four-input approximate-private exact SATE decision problem.
